verdict_text:
YES

The plan matches the specification. The delete pattern `gpt_neox\.layers\.(2|6|10|14)\.` removes exactly the 60 tensors of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14 (guarded by a count assert), and the ten `move` transforms implement the required mapping 3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 7→5, 8→6, 9→7, 11→8, 12→9, 13→10, 15→11 in ascending destination order, so every destination index is already vacated (by the delete or by an earlier move) before it is written — no collision. The regexes are anchored by the literal `gpt_neox.layers.` prefix and a trailing `\.`, so e.g. `layers.1.` cannot match `layers.11.` and `layers.(...|10|...)` cannot match `layers.12.`; the `\1` backreferences are in single-quoted YAML, so they survive as literal capture references, and names, values, shapes and dtypes are otherwise untouched. All three required checks are present after the renumbering: `not exists` for blocks 12–15, exactly 12 `query_key_value.weight` matches, and a total count of 184 (244 − 60), all as `assert` transforms so the run aborts before writing output if they fail.
